closed_add.name: CROWDE
closed_add.sector: Agritech — P2P lending and input financing for smallholder farmers
closed_add.why: CROWDE, set up in 2016 by Yohanes Sugihtononugroho and Muhamad Risyad Ganis, financed farmers' working capital through an OJK-licensed lending platform. OJK revoked its licence by KEP-68/D.06/2025 on 6 November 2025 for breaching the minimum-equity rule and deteriorating performance after earlier sanctions up to a business freeze, and failed its president director in a fit-and-proper reassessment. The funding figure is the US$1M pre-Series A led by Mandiri Capital Indonesia (Sep 2019); the 2018 GREE Ventures seed was undisclosed, and a 2021 round led by Monk's Hill that DealStreetAsia reported at US$7M was never announced with an amount, so it is not summed. The agri-nationwide group also lists this closure (founded 2015 there; Forbes says 2016).

closed_add.name: Pitik
closed_add.sector: Agritech — broiler-farm management, inputs and offtake for smallholder poultry farmers
closed_add.why: Pitik ran a full-stack broiler-chicken platform (IoT farm management, chick and feed supply, offtake) for smallholder farmers in Java, launched in mid-2021 by Arief Witjaksono and Rymax Joehana from an office on Jl. BSD Raya Utama. It raised an undisclosed seed round co-led by Arise and Wavemaker Partners (Dec 2021) and a US$14M Series A led by Alpha JWC Ventures (May 2022); only the Series A amount is counted. DealStreetAsia reported in April 2024 that it had laid off more than half its staff and on 13 July 2024 that it had ceased operations; youngster.id's December 2025 account says operations shut completely in April 2024. The company never announced the closure itself; pitik.id now shows a 'Domain Expired' page (checked 2026-09-28), and its LinkedIn page still lists 97 people from profiles that were not updated.

closed_add.name: TaniFund
closed_add.sector: Fintech — P2P lending for farmers (TaniHub Group)
closed_add.why: TaniFund was the P2P lending arm of TaniHub Group, financing farmers' working capital from 2017. After lender losses (its 90-day repayment rate stood near 36% in December 2022), OJK revoked its licence by KEP-19/D.06/2024 on 3 May 2024 for failing the minimum-equity rule and not carrying out supervisory recommendations; shareholders then voted to dissolve it and a liquidation team was formed (OJK, October 2024). Rounds were raised at TaniHub Group level, so no TaniFund figure is recorded. The parent TaniHub collapsed too but has no dated shutdown (see rejected).

closed_add.name: TaniHub
closed_add.sector: Agritech — farm-produce sourcing and distribution to business buyers (earlier also consumers)
closed_add.why: TaniHub (PT Tani Hub Indonesia, the trading arm of TaniHub Group alongside TaniFund) was a Jakarta agritech founded in 2015 that bought produce from farmers and sold it to businesses and, until 1 March 2022, to consumers; it reportedly raised a US$65.5M Series B in 2021 led by MDI Ventures. It closed its B2C service and its Bandung and Bali warehouses in March 2022, faced a PKPU (debt-suspension) petition in December 2022, and its lending arm TaniFund lost its OJK licence in May 2024. On 18 June 2026 the Jakarta Corruption Court sentenced its former CEO and former finance director, along with former MDI Ventures and BRI Ventures executives, over US$25M of state-linked investment; CNA describes TaniHub as having collapsed. No dated shutdown announcement was found, so the end month is left null; tanihub.com no longer responds (checked 2026-09-28).

closed_add.name: Qlapa
closed_add.sector: Commerce — online marketplace for Indonesian handmade crafts
closed_add.why: Qlapa was a marketplace for locally made handicrafts, founded in 2015 by Benny Fajarai and Fransiskus Xaverius and run by PT Qlapa Kreasi Bangsa. Management announced on its site and social accounts that the service closed on Saturday 2 March 2019 because it could not become a profitable, sustainable business. Its seed round (Global Founders Capital, Ideosource, Jan 2016) and Series A led by Aavishkaar Frontier Funds (Mar 2017) were both undisclosed, so no funding figure is recorded. qlapa.com no longer resolves (checked 2026-09-28).

closed_add.name: Stoqo
closed_add.sector: Commerce — B2B marketplace supplying rice, oil, flour and fresh ingredients to small restaurants
closed_add.why: Stoqo sold staple and fresh ingredients to small food businesses and employed about 250 people (Bloomberg). In late April 2020 it posted a notice on stoqo.com that it was stopping operations after COVID-19 restrictions cut restaurant demand; the notice called the stop temporary, its last day of operation was 22 April 2020 (CNBC) and it never reopened. Its Series A (Dec 2018, Monk's Hill Ventures and Accel) was undisclosed, so no funding figure is recorded. Founding year is 2017 per the company's job-board profile; PitchBook gives 2016.

closed_add.name: Airy
closed_add.sector: Travel — budget-hotel network and online booking (virtual hotel operator)
closed_add.why: Airy (Airy Rooms) partnered with budget hotels across Indonesia and sold rooms and flights through its own app; it was set up in 2015 by former Traveloka staff. The operator, PT Airy Nest Indonesia, stopped all operations including its property partnerships on 31 May 2020 because of the pandemic, and CEO Louis Alfonso Kodoatie confirmed that hundreds of staff were let go. airyrooms.com still shows only a farewell page ('Terima kasih Indonesia, Airy mohon pamit!', checked 2026-09-28). closed_add.name: Sorabel (Sale Stock)

Management told staff in a letter that employment would end on 30 July 2020 and that the company would file for liquidation after the pandemic cut sales and left it without a cash buffer; co-founder Jeffrey Yuwono confirmed the closure. The funding figure is the US$27M Series B+ announced in Aug 2017 (Gobi Partners and Golden Equator Capital); the 2019 pre-Series C (Kejora-Intervest, Shift) was undisclosed and earlier rounds are not summed. OJK revoked its licence and listed it as the one revocation in its register of licensed lenders dated 2 March 2022 (published 16 March); former staff said salaries and income tax had gone unpaid since late 2020, and FTI Consulting had been hired to restructure. Its August 2017 Series A of up to US$12M (K2 Venture Capital, Enspire, Alpha JWC, Draper Associates) mixed debt and equity without a published split, so no equity figure is recorded. uangteman.com now redirects to an unrelated gambling site.

closed_add.why: Bananas ran an app-based quick-commerce grocery service launched in January 2022 by ex-Lazada executive Mario Gaw (CEO) and Kristian Sinaulan (CTO); 2022 is its launch year. In mid-October 2022 it announced on Instagram that it was closing the service after ten months because the e-grocery business was not viable, sold off its stock and said the team would move to a new business; no successor product has been identified. The funding figure is its US$1.5M seed (Feb 2022): US$1M led by East Ventures with SMDV, ARISE, MDI Ventures and angels, plus US$500K from Y Combinator. No PT name was found.

closed_add.name: Lummo (BukuKas)
closed_add.sector: SaaS — digital bookkeeping and online-store tools for small merchants
closed_add.why: BukuKas, founded in December 2019 by Krishnan Menon and Lorenzo Peracchione and renamed Lummo in January 2022, gave small merchants a digital ledger and online-shop tools. closed_add.name: Tumbasin

closed_add.why: KitaBeli, launched in Jakarta in March 2020 by Prateek Chaturvedi and Ivana Tjandra, sold everyday goods through neighbourhood group-buying and expanded to Solo and Malang. No funding amounts were ever announced, so none is recorded, and pegipegi.com no longer resolves. Its corporate backing makes it a borderline case for the census's venture test.

The funding figure sums the US$19M Series A (Nov 2021, AppWorks and AC Ventures) and the US$13.5M pre-Series B bridge (Jan 2023, led by Telkomsel Mitra Inovasi); the 2019 seed is not counted. Marked reported: the company announced no shutdown.

closed_add.name: Zipmex Indonesia
closed_add.sector: Crypto — crypto-asset exchange (Indonesian arm of the Zipmex group)
closed_add.why: Zipmex Indonesia was the local exchange of the Singapore- and Thailand-based Zipmex group; it was registered with Bappebti as a prospective crypto trader in February 2020 and launched publicly in June 2021. After the group froze withdrawals in July 2022, Bappebti said in June 2024 that PT Zipmex Exchange Indonesia had applied two to three months earlier to close and was returning customer assets, and in September 2024 that it expected the closure to be completed that year. The last trading day was not published, so 2024-06 is the month the regulator confirmed the shutdown. Funding was raised at group level, so no Indonesian figure is recorded.

closed_add.name: Investree
closed_add.sector: Fintech — P2P lending for SMEs (invoice and working-capital financing)
closed_add.why: Investree was one of Indonesia's largest SME lenders. OJK revoked its licence by KEP-53/D.06/2024 on 21 October 2024 for breaching the minimum-equity rule and other provisions amid worsening performance; the company, now in liquidation, publishes dissolution and claims notices on investree.id, and former CEO Adrian Gunadi was arrested in September 2025 (CNBC). The funding figure sums the US$23.5M first tranche of its Series C (Apr 2020, MUIP and BRI Ventures) and the US$231M Series D announced in October 2023 through its Singapore parent with Qatar's JTA; the 2018 Series B amount was not found and earlier rounds are not summed.

closed_add.name: GetPlus
closed_add.sector: Marketing tech — multi-brand coalition loyalty and rewards programme
closed_add.why: GetPlus was a coalition loyalty programme run by PT Global Poin Indonesia, with 500+ partner merchants and over a million members, relaunched on Antavo's platform in January 2023. It announced on its official Instagram on 14 October 2024 that point redemption would end on 20 October and that the service would stop operating on 6 December 2024, without giving a reason. It was backed by GDP Venture but no round amounts were announced, so no funding figure is recorded; getplus.id no longer resolves.

closed_add.name: Gravel
closed_add.sector: Proptech — on-demand marketplace for construction workers and building projects
closed_add.why: Gravel, founded in Jakarta in 2019 by Georgi Ferdwindra Putra, Fredy Yanto and Nicholas Sutardja, matched contractors and property owners with vetted construction workers and claimed 25,000 workers across 18 provinces by 2022. A year after raising US$14M led by New Enterprise Associates with SMDV and East Ventures (Dec 2023), it collapsed: youngster.id and The Runway (Oct 2025) put the end in December 2024, with the website offline and workers unpaid, and blame a split between the two co-CEOs. The company made no announcement, so this is marked reported; the funding figure is the US$14M round only, and gravel.co.id no longer resolves.

closed_add.name: Ula
closed_add.sector: Commerce — B2B wholesale marketplace and working capital for warung retailers
closed_add.why: Ula, launched in January 2020 by Nipun Mehra and co-founders, supplied stock and credit to more than 100,000 warungs in Java. It left FMCG distribution in October 2023 and had largely paused operations by late 2023; in February 2025 it announced a wind-down, with Mehra saying in a statement that investors could redeem at about 30% of capital raised or roll into his next venture, and by July 2025 only the founders and a new entity remained on the cap table. The funding figure sums the US$10.5M seed (Jun 2020), US$20M Series A (Jan 2021) and US$87M Series B (Oct 2021); reports put the total above US$140M, and the rest is not summed. ula.app now describes the business in the past tense; no PT name was found.

closed_add.name: Octopus
closed_add.sector: Climate — recycling and reverse-logistics app connecting households, waste collectors and FMCG brands
closed_add.city: Kota Makassar (founding base; later ran a Jakarta Pusat office)
closed_add.why: Octopus was a post-consumer waste collection startup that began in Makassar (a 2020 HighPitch winner there) and raised US$5 million in July 2022 from Openspace, SOSV and others. From December 2023 it failed to pay staff and waste-collector partners. DealStreetAsia reported the unpaid salaries and governance allegations in January 2024, and a co-founder left in February 2024. A June 2024 report was headlined 'Octopus sinks amid unpaid staff wages, stalled acquisition talks' (paywalled; the headline is indexed on parsers.vc), and Uzone reported in July 2024 that wages were still unpaid and co-founders unreachable. No formal bankruptcy or company statement was found, and its domain octopus.co.id no longer resolves (DNS lame delegation, checked 2026-09-28). The Indonesian legal entity was not verified; LinkedIn shows a Singapore holdco, Octopus Waste Management Pte Ltd.
